## What's Changed

- Added a Windows 10+ amd64 preview zip with `statlite.exe`, a short Windows
  README and a ready-to-use self-monitoring configuration. Windows runs as a
  console application; local host CPU, memory and disk metrics remain unavailable.
- Clarify first-run self-monitoring setup for binary installs and keep Windows
  setup instructions in a dedicated guide.
- Added a Telegram health-notification recipe using the external API, with
  recovery notices and application health details.
- Requir

- CI passed native Go tests, storage integration, static analysis, dashboard tests, and startup, Spring collection, graceful shutdown, SQLite integrity, preserved history, and restart checks on Windows Server 2022. Other integrations have not been individually certified on Windows.
This preview provides the same application monitoring, configuration, SQLite history, and browser dashboard functionality as StatLite 0.7, with the Windows limitations described below. It runs as a foreground console application

## What's Changed

- Added first-class Caddy HTTP monitoring for one exact hostname per target,
  using native `per_host` metrics from Caddy 2.11.4. Existing charts show
  requests, HTTP errors, and average response time without application
  instrumentation. Collection success does not establish upstream application
  health; application runtime and dependency health remain unavailable.
- Added Caddy setup guidance for same-server and private Docker deployments,
  plus a public integration smoke journey co

## What's Changed

- Improved 7-day and 30-day dashboard chart performance with bounded sampling.
  These charts are approximate overviews and can miss intermediate spikes or
  counter resets; raw stored history remains authoritative.
- Added `--raw-series` for troubleshooting chart optimizations by returning the
  full-resolution series within the effective requested range without dashboard
  sampling or aggregation.

Faster screens, waiting calls answered one at a time, and a summary of what came in while you were away.

- **Faster everywhere.** Activity reads only the channels your setup follows (on one Mac, 2 pages instead of 19 to open the month), and each account's saved record is read once instead of on every screen refresh: accounts, guru pages and the account feed answer in tens of milliseconds instead of hundreds.
- **Waiting calls, one at a time.** The calls waiting for you open as a queue on the account page:

Follow the guru's stops if you choose to, Activity totals you can trust, and a missed buy caught.

- **Follow the guru's stops (off by default).** Turn on **Follow the guru's stops** in an account's limits, and when the guru posts a stop ("跌破50.95出剩下的保护", "止损放38.4"), CopyTrading places a stop order at Alpaca for the shares it bought on that buy, never your own. A copied sell shrinks the stop or ends it, a newer stop replaces it, and a stop that fills is recorded as a sell from that buy

Polish on the new app: one icon set, motion that settles quickly, a calendar and steppers where you type, and gurus compared side by side.

- **Gurus compared side by side.** With two or more gurus, Gurus is a table: the accounts each copies into, whether it's copying, posts today with traded and waiting counts, win rate, realized profit with its trend, and open profit, sorted by realized profit. With one guru, Gurus still opens their page.

**A new CopyTrading.** The app is rebuilt from the ground up: the same engine, trading rules, setup, and history, in a faster, clearer desktop app with a dark trading-desk look. Your setup, accounts, and records carry over; on first launch it copies your saved keys from the old app once, so macOS asks whether CopyTrading may read them (choose **Always Allow**).

- **An account page that reads at a glance.** Balance and today's change, cash, buying power, what CopyTrading invested, and the calls waiting for

Every screen redrawn on one calmer design, a page for each stock, and Activity no longer flashes while it loads.

- **One design across the app.** Accounts, Activity, gurus, Settings, Connections, Getting Started and the Assistant share the same type, spacing, cards and controls, in dark (the default) and light.
